chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Sama'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman with irregular menstruation (mustahadha). He said, 'She fasts the month of Ramadan except for the days in which she used to menstruate, then she makes them up afterwards.'

key_terms.تَقْضِيهَا: She makes them up (makes up missed fasts)

ai.seo_question: How does a woman with irregular menstruation (istihadha) calculate her fasting and make-up days in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istihadha* where a woman retains her regular menstrual cycle pattern despite irregular bleeding, allowing her to fast Ramadan while excluding only those historically recognized days. It highlights the Shia juristic reliance on identifying a 'habitual' period to distinguish between *hayd* (menstruation) and *istihadha*, ensuring the validity of her worship. The ruling underscores the practical application of consistency in ritual purity laws for women navigating prolonged or irregular bleeding.
